cover.title: How extreme rain causes floods
cover.subtitle: When heavy downpours overwhelm ancient storm drains and wetlands vanish, water piles up. Discover the physics of fluid pressure.
cover.subject: Physics · Pressure
cover.fun_fact: A water depth of just 0.50 m exerts a crushing pressure of 4,900 pascals on surfaces below!
story.title: When drains and wetlands vanish
story.lead: On November 6, a heavy downpour flooded Colombo within minutes, stranding commuters [1]. Century-old storm drains could not keep up with the extreme rain [1].
story.image_caption: Archive photo · Red Dragon scuplture during River Lee flooding, October
stat.1.label: rainfall per hour during the flash flood
stat.2.label: hourly capacity of the old storm drains
stat.3.label: rainwater retained by natural wetlands
story.body_1: Rainwater rushed through Colombo's streets when hourly rainfall exceeded 120 mm [1]. The century-old drainage system was designed for only 30 mm per hour [1]. As real estate development replaces natural wetlands and green spaces, rainwater has nowhere to absorb safely [1].
story.body_2: Wetlands act as natural sponges that hold excess water and protect cities [1]. Environmental experts warn that restoring wetlands and upgrading drainage are vital for urban climate resilience [1].
timeline.1.text: Wetlands and drains are clear and ready.
timeline.2.text: Rain falls faster than drains can carry away.
timeline.3.text: Water pools on streets, building high pressure.
physics.title: Water pressure and depth
physics.body_1: Standing water exerts pressure on everything beneath it. The deeper the water gets, the greater the pressure pushes down and sideways [2].
physics.body_2: Fluid pressure depends on water density, gravity, and depth. This relationship is calculated using the hydrostatic pressure formula [2].
physics.assumptions: We assume water density is constant and ignore atmospheric pressure for the fluid column.
table.note: Greater depth creates much higher water pressure.

lab.title: Water depth and pressure test
lab.step_1: Fill a tall clear plastic bottle with water up to different depth marks.
lab.step_2: Measure the height h with a ruler.
lab.step_3: Calculate p = ρgh for each depth using 1,000 kg/m³.
